elements.content: Grammar focus: Formal and Informal Register.

Decide the audience, then adjust all four axes at once. Formalising only the vocabulary and leaving contractions produces a letter that reads as uncertain, and formalising only the grammar leaves phrasal verbs that sound out of place.

lexis — Latinate verb instead of phrasal: obtain, not get; resolve, not sort out
grammar — no contractions, full forms: we will, not we'll
requests — conditional and indirect: I would be grateful if you could…
distance — impersonal subject: the report indicates, not I think
density — nominalisation: the implementation of the policy
hedging — softened claims: this would appear to be the case
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which is the formal version of 'We'll look into it'?
2. Which request is most formal?
options: I would be grateful if you could send the file.

elements.content: 3. What does formal register NOT require?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

Informal — We'll sort it out next week. (Contracted, phrasal, short.)
Formal — We will resolve the matter next week. (No contraction, Latinate verb.)
Informal — Can you check this? (Direct question.)
Formal — I would be grateful if you could check this. (Indirect, softened.)
What do you observe?

Register shifts on four axes: vocabulary (get / obtain, help / assist), grammar (contractions, phrasal verbs, question forms), distance (I want / I would like; direct order / indirect request) and length (one clause or a nominalised phrase). Formal English avoids contractions, prefers single Latinate verbs to phrasal verbs, and puts requests in the conditional.
1. Which is more formal?
options: We would like to obtain the data.
We want to get the data.

elements.content: 2. Are contractions always wrong in formal writing?
options: No: they are avoided, not forbidden, in most formal prose.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can compare formal and informal register.

Success criteria:
- I can move a sentence up and down the register scale.
- I can make a request formal without making it ungrammatical.
- I can keep one register inside a single message.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ I want that you send the file (formal vocabulary, ungrammatical pattern) → ✅ I would like you to send the file
❌ We regret to inform you that we can't come (mixed register within one sentence) → ✅ We regret to inform you that we are unable to attend
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

I would be grateful if you could confirm receipt by Friday.
Unfortunately, we are unable to attend on that date.
Sorry, we can't make it on the 12th.

- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
